subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw accept a custom yielding walker as the canonical `bootstrap-extra-files` glob implementation, with its tested Node-glob parity contract, rather than preserve native `fs.glob` behavior?
rationale: The patch addresses a real responsiveness problem and preserves public SDK signatures, but its central mechanism intentionally replaces a runtime dependency’s behavior on existing user configuration. That compatibility boundary needs owner intent rather than an automated merge decision.

options.title: Accept the walker contract
options.body: Approve the cooperative walker after rebasing and validating the documented parity cases on the current merge result.

options.title: Narrow the approach
options.body: Keep async root reads and hook yields, but pursue a smaller native-glob-compatible scheduling strategy if maintainers do not want OpenClaw to own glob semantics.

recommendation.title: Accept the walker contract
recommendation.body: Approve the cooperative walker after rebasing and validating the documented parity cases on the current merge result.
